newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peru's Fujimori says hostage crisis can be solved.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Fujimori says hostage crisis can be solved.

text.p: Peru's President Alberto Fujimori said on Tuesday the Lima hostage crisis could be resolved without violence but insisted the Marxist guerrillas lay down their arms and free all 83 people they are holding.
"I believe that in the end reason will impose a solution without the spilling of blood..," Fujimori told the Spanish news agency EFE in his first public statement on the crisis for 10 days.
He added however, that for his government to "rule out the use of force" the guerrillas must "lay down their arms and proceed with the liberation of all the hostages."

In the interview, made available to Reuters in Madrid, Fujimori reiterated that while his government was keeping up dialogue with the hostage-takers it ruled out "any possibility of freeing the jailed militants of the MRTA" -- one of the guerrillas' original demands.
Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels seized the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima in a spectacular raid on December 17.

The guerrillas have freed more than 420 hostages since they took over the building, but 83 still remained captive, including three ambassadors, dozens of Japanese businessmen and most of the top officials of Peru's police and intelligence forces.

Fujimori, when asked whether his government might pardon the hostage-takers, said: "My government cannot forecast the outcome. Nevertheless, I repeat, there is the greatest will to reach a peaceful, reasonable, civilised solution."
He added: "One can think of several options. These are the basis for the conversations."
